title: Manual unlink of dest/.parquet.tmp in _write_chunk_checkpoint failure path is unreachable-as-effective; atomic_write already guarantees removal
description: On a checkpoint write failure, _write_chunk_checkpoint's except block calls `path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` and `path.with_suffix('.parquet.tmp').unlink(missing_ok=True)` before rmdir. Neither call can ever find a file to remove. `atomic_write` (src/haute/_polars_utils.py:288-293) wraps the write in `try: yield tmp; tmp.replace(dest) except BaseException: tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True); raise`, so on ANY exception inside the `with` body (the only failure point is `frame.write_parquet(tmp, ...)`) the temp file is already unlinked by atomic_write before control returns to _write_chunk_checkpoint. The final `dest` is created only by the atomic `tmp.replace(dest)`, which runs solely on the success path and is itself atomic (os.replace cannot partially create dest), so `path` (dest) never exists on the failure path either. Thus both unlink calls are guaranteed no-ops. The only load-bearing cleanup in this block is the `checkpoint_dir.rmdir()` (which removes the now-empty owned dir on a first-chunk failure). The redundant unlinks are confirmed non-load-bearing by the passing regression test test_chunk_runner_cleans_partial_checkpoint_write_failure (tests/test_chunk_runner.py:890-914), which writes a partial tmp file then raises and still passes purely via atomic_write's own cleanup.
evidence: _polars_utils.py atomic_write: `try: yield tmp; tmp.replace(dest) except BaseException: tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True); raise` -> tmp always removed on failure, dest never created on failure. chunking.py:1552-1556: `with atomic_write(path) as tmp: frame.write_parquet(...) except BaseException: path.unlink(missing_ok=True); path.with_suffix('.parquet.tmp').unlink(missing_ok=True); ...` -> at this point tmp is already gone and dest absent, so both unlinks match nothing in every reachable path (write_parquet failure, or the atomic replace failure).
est_reduction: -2 LOC (drop the two redundant unlink statements at 1555-1556; keep the rmdir cleanup). Net: removes dead defensive cleanup, leaving atomic_write as the single source of temp/dest cleanup.
behavior_preservation: Behavior is identical: the two unlinks are provable no-ops in all reachable failure paths because atomic_write unconditionally unlinks the temp file and never creates dest on failure. The kept rmdir and the outer _cleanup_written_checkpoints path are unaffected. test_chunk_runner_cleans_partial_checkpoint_write_failure already proves cleanup succeeds without relying on these unlinks.
